description: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center - Large Item Scrap Processing and Removal Term Contract IFB No. 2-1-QSC-T-26-112 AMENDMENT (1) NOTIFICATION � AUGUST 26, 2026 Amendment (1) has been issued for IFB No. 2-1-QSC-T-26-112. Prospective bidders are advised that the solicitation package has been revised to address stormwater and environmental permitting requirements, post-bid/pre-award documentation, Performance Guarantee timing, NASA Marshall Space Flight Center environmental coordination, and site access and inspection procedures. Among the revisions, the Apparent Successful Bidder will be required to obtain separate coverage under Alabama Department of Environmental Management (ADEM) General Permit ALG180000 � Salvage/Recycling as a condition of final contract award. Required bidder-controlled post-bid/pre-award actions, including applicable documentation, environmental coordination, permit submission activities, and the Performance Guarantee, are generally required within fifteen (15) business days after written notification that the bidder is the Apparent Successful Bidder, as provided in the amended IFB. Prospective bidders must review Amendment (1), the amended IFB, and all revised solicitation documents in their entirety before submitting a bid. Bidders are responsible for acknowledging Amendment (1) in accordance with the IFB. The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is soliciting sealed bids for a Large Item Scrap Processing and Removal Term Contract for Government-owned DEMIL A scrap located at NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, Alabama. This is a project-driven term contract. Individual scrap processing and removal projects will be assigned to the awarded Contractor through Project Authorizations issued during the contract term. Projects may vary substantially in size, complexity, schedule, location, equipment requirements, and method of execution. Property may include large industrial equipment, aerospace hardware, test articles, pressure vessels, tanks, structural steel assemblies, manufacturing equipment, fabrication scrap, launch vehicle or propulsion-related hardware, obsolete machinery, oversized ferrous and non-ferrous scrap, and other Government-owned scrap designated for disposition. Projects may require dismantling, torch cutting, mechanical size reduction, rigging, crane operations, heavy lifting, loading, transportation preparation, removal, and incidental site cleanup and restoration. Bidders shall submit a single fixed unit purchase price in dollars per pound ($/lb) representing the amount the Contractor will pay the Government for each verified pound of Government-owned property removed under the Contract. IMPORTANT DATES - CENTRAL TIME (CT) IFB Issuance: August 20, 2026 Amendment (1) Issued: August 26, 2026 Deadline for Questions: September 18, 2026 Bid Submission Deadline: September 21, 2026 - 5:00 PM CT Public Bid Opening: September 23, 2026 - 9:00 AM CT Anticipated Pre-Award Date: September 25, 2026 MANDATORY PRE-BID SITE INSPECTION A pre-bid site inspection is mandatory. Prospective bidders are encouraged to begin the inspection scheduling and access-approval process as early as possible. Certain access requests, including those involving Lawful Permanent Residents, foreign nationals, or other non-routine access, may require additional processing time and security approval. Failure to obtain required access and complete the mandatory pre-bid site inspection may result in a bid being determined non-responsive. The fifteen-business-day requirement applies to actions within the bidder's control. ADEM processing time following a timely and complete submission does not, by itself, make the bidder delinquent. Active ALG180000 coverage is required before final contract award. Refer to the amended IFB and Marshall SWPP Permit Procedures for complete requirements. PERFORMANCE GUARANTEE The Apparent Successful Bidder will be required to furnish a $60,000 Performance Guarantee within fifteen (15) business days after written notification that it is the Apparent Successful Bidder. The Performance Guarantee must be received and approved by the Government before final contract award. Refer to Section 5.2 of the IFB for complete requirements. description: NASA Marshall Space Flight Center - Large Item Scrap Processing and Removal Term Contract IFB No. 2-1-QSC-T-26-112 The U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) is soliciting sealed bids for a Large Item Scrap Processing and Removal Term Contract for Government-owned DEMIL A scrap located at NASA Marshall Space Flight Center (MSFC), Huntsville, Alabama. title: MT0055AW, 34406, Roof and Building Envelope Modernization, Turner LPOE - Amendment 0001
description: Amendment 0001 is to update the solicitation with the following change: 1. Site Visit is scheduled for August 18, 2026, at 1:00 PM Mountain Time. Location: Turner LPOE 41725 Turner Rd Turner, MT 59542 2. RSVP for the site visit by August 13, 2026 to Mark Lovie at mark.lovie@gsa.gov. His cell number is (415)961-0222. Ensure you CC' john.morelion@gsa.gov. 3. RFI's will be due August 26, 2026. 4. Offers will be due September 03, 2026 by 4:30PM MST. All Offer should be emailed to john.morelion@gsa.gov Please be reminded to bring your verification of ID to the site visit. The amendment will be an attachment include a signed copy with your offer. The U.S. General Services Administration intends to solicit construction services for the Turner Roof & Building Envelope Project at the Turner Land Port of Entry, 41725 Turner Road, Turner, Montana 59542, Building No. MT0055AW. The project includes roof replacement and building envelope improvements at the main building, including work on the U.S. and Canadian sides of the facility, and envelope improvements at the water treatment building. Work includes, but is not limited to, selective demolition, roof replacement, exterior wall/cladding repairs, thermal and moisture protection, metals, openings, finishes, and incidental electrical, communications, and securityrelated coordination. The facility will remain occupied and operational during construction. The contractor must phase and secure the work daily, maintain safe access, protect ongoing border operations, and coordinate with GSA, CBP, CBSA, and other stakeholders regarding antennas, cameras, cables, signs, access, security, and inspections. Work affecting the Canadian side may require Canadian access, work permit, and material import coordination.Certain roofing materials may be furnished through the existing roofing warranty process; the contractor will be responsible for coordinating those materials with the manufacturer/certified installer and providing all remaining labor, materials, equipment, supervision, bonds, permits, and incidentals required to complete the work. The contractor shall comply with the solicitation documents, drawings, specifications, applicable codes and standards, GSA PBS Core Building Standards, security and badging requirements, environmental survey requirements, fire/life safety requirements, submittal requirements, and closeout requirements. The anticipated period of performance is 150 calendar days after notice to proceed. The solicitation is expected to include base bid work for the main building roof and envelope on the U.S. side, main building roof and envelope on the Canadian side, and water treatment building envelope work on the U.S. side.
